node.title: Canonical high-core component-union atlas
node.statement: For a generic post-strip pair, graph live slopes by size-k collisions, equivalently by witness error-set unions of size R=n-k. The nonisolated slopes partition into canonical connected components C. A lexicographic spanning-tree selection chooses one witness ray per slope and a component union U_C of size R+d_C. Each slope has an r=n-A supported lift in U_C, genericity is inherited, and GRK gives |Z_C|C(d_C+h,d_C)<=C(R+d_C,d_C)R. Hence the high-core slope count is the exact disjoint sum over C and is at most sum_C floor(C(R+d_C,d_C)R/C(d_C+h,d_C)). This resolves core/chart/slope deduplication but does not bound the component count or excess ledger by 8n^3.
